items.title: /init
items.summary: Scan the project and write a CLAUDE.md the agent reads in every future session.
items.detail: The single highest-leverage first command in a new repo. It documents build/test commands, architecture and conventions into CLAUDE.md, which is loaded automatically every session after that. Re-run it after a big structural change.

items.title: /resume  ·  claude -r  ·  claude -c
items.summary: Pick up an old session with its full context instead of re-explaining yourself.
items.detail: /resume lists past sessions to jump back into. From the shell, `claude -c` continues the most recent conversation and `claude -r` resumes a chosen one. Context, file state and decisions come back with it.
items.snippet:
/resume

# or from the shell
claude -c        # continue latest
claude -r        # pick a session

items.title: /clear  vs  /compact
items.summary: Two different resets — using the wrong one costs you either context or money.
items.detail: /clear wipes the conversation entirely: right when you switch to an unrelated task. /compact summarises the conversation so far and keeps going: right when you're deep in one task and running long. Reaching for /clear mid-task throws away hard-won context; never compacting burns tokens on stale history.
items.snippet:
/clear      # new task, forget everything
/compact    # same task, summarise and continue

items.title: /agents
items.summary: Create and manage subagents — separate context windows with their own tools and prompt.
items.detail: Subagents live in .claude/agents/*.md with frontmatter for name, description, tools and model. They keep a focused job (reviewer, explorer, test-writer) out of your main context window, which is the real win: your conversation stays clean while the grunt work happens elsewhere.

items.title: /mcp
items.summary: Connect external tools — issue trackers, databases, browsers — as first-class tools.
items.detail: Manages MCP server connections and OAuth for them. Project-scoped servers belong in .mcp.json checked into the repo so the whole team gets the same tools; personal ones stay in user scope.

items.title: /permissions
items.summary: Allow the safe stuff once so you stop answering the same prompt forty times a day.
items.detail: Opens the permission rules editor. Allowlist the read-only commands you run constantly (git status, ls, npm test) and keep destructive ones on ask. This is the fix for prompt fatigue — not --dangerously-skip-permissions.

items.title: /hooks
items.summary: Run your own shell commands automatically at defined points in the agent loop.
items.detail: Hooks fire deterministically — PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, SessionStart and more. The killer use is auto-formatting and linting after every edit: the agent can't forget, because the harness runs it, not the model.

items.title: /rewind  ·  Esc Esc
items.summary: Roll the conversation and your files back to an earlier checkpoint.
items.detail: Checkpoints are taken as the agent edits, so a run that went sideways is recoverable without git gymnastics. Double-tap Esc to jump back and edit an earlier message, or /rewind to restore code, conversation, or both.
items.snippet:
/rewind

# or press Esc twice to edit an earlier turn

items.title: /memory  ·  #
items.summary: Edit CLAUDE.md, or prefix a line with # to save a rule mid-conversation.
items.detail: /memory opens the memory files for editing. The faster path: start any message with # and the agent files it into memory for you. Use it the moment you correct the same thing twice.
items.snippet: # always run pnpm, never npm, in this repo

items.title: /model
items.summary: Swap models mid-session — heavier for design, lighter for mechanical work.
items.detail: Switch without losing the conversation. A common rhythm: a strong model to plan and decide, a faster one to grind through the mechanical edits the plan produced.

items.title: Custom slash commands
items.summary: A markdown file in .claude/commands/ becomes /your-command, arguments and all.
items.detail: The file body is the prompt. $ARGUMENTS (or $1, $2) interpolates what the user typed; frontmatter sets allowed-tools and a description; a !`shell command` line injects live output into the prompt. Project commands are shared via git, personal ones live in ~/.claude/commands.
items.snippet:
# .claude/commands/fix-issue.md
---
description: Fix a GitHub issue end to end
allowed-tools: Bash(gh:*), Read, Edit
---
Fix issue #$ARGUMENTS. Start by reading it: !`gh issue view $ARGUMENTS`

items.title: claude -p
items.summary: Headless print mode: one prompt in, structured answer out, no TUI.
items.detail: The bridge between the agent and every script you already have. Accepts piped stdin, supports --output-format json|stream-json, and honours --allowedTools for a tight sandbox. This is what CI jobs, git hooks and cron tasks call.
items.snippet: git diff | claude -p "Summarise this change in one paragraph" --output-format json

items.title: /cost  ·  /usage
items.summary: See what the session actually cost before the invoice does it for you.
items.detail: /cost reports token usage and spend for the current session; /usage shows plan limits. Pair with /compact discipline — most runaway cost is stale context being re-sent every turn.

items.title: /add-dir
items.summary: Bring a second repo into the session without restarting in a parent folder.
items.detail: Grants access to an additional working directory mid-session — the clean way to work across a frontend and backend repo at once, or to reference a sibling library while editing your service.

items.title: /doctor  ·  /bug
items.summary: Check the install's health, or send a bug report with session context attached.
items.detail: /doctor diagnoses installation, auth and config problems — the first thing to run when something behaves strangely. /bug files a report to Anthropic including the conversation context, which makes it actually actionable.
